# The Colors That Dance in the Dark

## Scripture
"The heavens declare the glory of God; the skies proclaim the work of his hands." — Psalm 19:1 (NIV)

## Reflection
In the fall, as darkness stretches longer across the northern skies, something remarkable happens: the aurora borealis begins to dance. Charged particles from the sun, hurled across millions of miles, collide with Earth's atmosphere and burst into curtains of green, violet, and rose. The darker the night, the more brilliant the display.

Here is the wonder: those colors don't come from the sky itself. They come from something far away—the sun's invisible breath reaching across the void—meeting the protective embrace of Earth's magnetic field. The aurora is a picture of glory born from distance and defense, light that travels far to find us.

Psalm 19 says the heavens *declare*—they don't whisper. God's glory isn't hidden in some quiet corner of creation; it shouts in color across the polar night. And notice: the aurora only appears when the dark is deep enough. God is not stymied by the long nights of our lives. He specializes in displays of glory that require darkness as their canvas.

If this season feels shadowed for you, take heart. The One who flings solar winds across space and catches them in Earth's磁场—sorry, in Earth's field—is the same God who holds you. Your long night is not wasted. It may be the very backdrop where His glory becomes most visible.

## Prayer
Father, when the nights grow long, remind me that Your glory shines brightest against the dark. Thank You for the aurora's witness—light that travels far, caught and held by Your design. Let my life declare Your handiwork, even in shadowed seasons. Amen.
